newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Granada sees early 97 Welcome Break sale.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Granada sees early 97 Welcome Break sale.

text.p: Granada Group chairman Gerry Robinson said on Wednesday that the company aimed to complete the sale of its Welcome Break motorway service areas in early 1997.

Robinson told Reuters in a telephone interview that he expected the sale to happen "in January or February". Granada acquired the 21 service areas as part of its takeover of Forte but must sell them because of monopoly concerns.
Robinson said that Granada would retain its holding of some 10.8 pct in television broadcaster BSkyB "for the foreseeable future".
"Our decision to hold on to the (BSkyB) stake looks like a good one from any angle," said Robinson, noting that its value had risen from some 600 million stg to around one billion in recent months.

Robinson, who is also chairman of BSkyB, said there was a lot of useful cross-over between the satellite broadcaster and Granada's own media business. Granada and BSkyB launched a series of satellite lifestyle channels in October under the Granada Sky Broadcasting joint venture.
Robinson declined to comment on Granada's plans regarding Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television.
Granada has built up a total stake of 27 percent in its northern neighbour Yorkshire and had been expected to make a full bid for the commercial ITV broadcaster at some point.

New media ownership legislation allows Granada to add to its two ITV franchises for north-west England and London Weekend Television. But it has yet to make its move for Yorkshire and some analysts believe it sees the share price as too high.

Granada's 1995/96 profit before tax and exceptional items rose 37 percent to 480 million stg. "The results are very satisfying. The key has been the speed with which we have been able to move on the Forte businesses," Robinson said.

Granada said it had already improved profitability by approaching 40 million stg at Forte and was confident that it would meet its target of improving ongoing profits by over 100 million stg per annum from 1996/97.
